clf-avc-091.text: A company wants application capacity to grow and shrink automatically according to workload demand so it avoids both overload and long periods of idle compute. Which AWS capability best implements this elasticity for EC2 fleets?
clf-avc-091.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of EC2 instances according to scaling policies and demand, helping maintain performance while reducing unnecessary idle capacity.
clf-avc-091.hint: Think of the service that changes fleet size automatically.
optionRationales: EC2 Auto Scaling provides dynamic fleet capacity.

clf-avc-092.text: A predictable workload reaches a traffic peak every weekday at exactly the same time. The team wants additional EC2 capacity to be ready before the traffic arrives instead of waiting for a metric alarm. Which Auto Scaling approach is most appropriate?
clf-avc-092.explanation: Scheduled Scaling changes Auto Scaling capacity at predefined times and is appropriate for recurring predictable demand patterns.
clf-avc-092.hint: The demand pattern is known in advance and follows the clock.
optionRationales: Scheduled Scaling prepares capacity before predictable peaks.
Target Tracking reacts to measured demand rather than the known schedule.
Manual scaling is unnecessary and error-prone.
S3 Lifecycle is unrelated to compute scaling.

clf-avc-093.text: A company wants an Auto Scaling group to keep average CPU utilization near a defined target such as 50%, automatically adjusting instance count as the metric changes. Which scaling policy is designed for this behavior?
clf-avc-093.explanation: Target Tracking Scaling adjusts capacity automatically to keep a selected metric close to a specified target value.
clf-avc-093.hint: The policy continuously follows a target metric value.
optionRationales: Target Tracking maintains a selected metric near a target.

clf-avc-094.text: A company wants a managed deployment platform where developers upload application code and AWS automatically provisions and manages resources such as EC2 instances, load balancing, and scaling while still exposing those resources for customization. Which service fits?
clf-avc-094.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk provides a managed application-platform experience that deploys code and provisions supporting infrastructure automatically.
clf-avc-094.hint: Think of the AWS PaaS-style application deployment service.

clf-avc-095.text: An infrastructure team wants every VPC, role, instance, and database defined in version-controlled YAML or JSON so identical environments can be recreated automatically. Which AWS service provides native infrastructure-as-code stacks?
clf-avc-095.explanation: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages AWS resources from declarative templates and organizes them into reproducible stacks.
clf-avc-095.hint: Think of the AWS service that turns infrastructure templates into stacks.
optionRationales: CloudFormation is AWS-native infrastructure as code.
Config records and evaluates configuration state.
AWS Support does not provision infrastructure from templates.

clf-avc-096.text: A company needs repeatable, automated software delivery from source through build, test, and deployment stages. Which AWS service is designed to orchestrate a CI/CD release pipeline?
clf-avc-096.explanation: AWS CodePipeline orchestrates continuous delivery workflows by connecting source, build, test, approval, and deployment stages.
clf-avc-096.hint: Think of the AWS pipeline service for software delivery.
